crag noun

also outcrop, rocky outcrop, jagged rock, tor

classical

Caes. BG 3.13: saxa et cautēs timēre (Lewis & Short)
Verg. A. 4.366: dūrae (Lewis & Short)
Ov. Met. 4.672 (Lewis & Short)

cautēs, cautis f.

noun, third declension

a rough, pointed rock

Akin to cōs, a whetstone: the sharp, jagged rock, where rūpēs is the sheer face. An outcrop has no one word; a rock that juts out is saxum prōminēns (Aelius Gallus in Festus, in Lewis & Short s.v. petra).

Examples

  • saxa et cautēs timēre

    to fear rocks and cragsCaes. BG 3.13 (Lewis & Short)

See also cliff, rock, mountain, flint.

SourcesLewis & Short: cautes · Lewis & Short: petra
